title: Western Red Cedar: Great Thujas You Can Visit
meta_description: A Pacific Northwest giant that layers into new trunks. The Duncan Cedar, the largest known in the world, is over 1,000 years old and mostly dead wood.
intro: Western red cedar grows to enormous size in the rainforests of the Pacific Northwest, and its wood resists rot so well that a tree can stay alive on a strip of bark. The Duncan Cedar, near Olympic National Park, is the largest known in the world and the largest tree of any species in Washington: over a thousand years old, 54 metres tall, and mostly dead wood. Planted abroad, it does something else. Its lowest branches bend under their own weight, touch the ground, root where they land and thicken into trunks of their own. Sintra's has been heading toward the lake below Pena Palace for about 150 years, and forestry students have used it as a teaching example since at least 1916. Strasbourg's is doing the same in the Parc de l'Orangerie. Cork's, at Blarney, sends out limbs each thicker than most full grown trees.
